patsnap.auth: claude.ai host connector: oauth-handshake-completed 2026-07-30 (operator-initiated). No API key on disk. A subprocess adapter would need PatSnap Eureka/Analytics API credentials, which are a paid commercial subscription — not provisioned.
patsnap.purpose: Global patent + academic-paper retrieval — the FIRST intellectual-property source in this stack. `patsnap_search` takes one source per call (`patent` default, or `paper`) under a strict strategy-to-parameter binding (semantic->semantic_query, keyword->keywords, filter->filters; each chosen strategy REQUIRES its parameter and its absence FORBIDS it). Filters cover assignee, inventor, IPC prefix, jurisdiction, legal status (active/inactive/pending), citation floor, and a date range over publication/application/granted/priority/expired. `patsnap_fetch` returns Markdown for up to 100 keys (patent URL, paper URL, or publication number) across four modules: basic, citation, legal, family. Verified live 2026-07-30: a US + A61K + active + 2022-onward GLP-1 query returned 50,447 hits with assignees, inventors, IPC, legal status, all four date fields, cited_count and full claim text per record.
patsnap.business_value: high — the only freedom-to-operate / IP-landscape capability in the stack; underwrites any founder-facing SKU. Chat-supervisory ONLY until the citation gap below is closed.
patsnap.suggested_adapter_path: openclaw-bridge/mcp/patsnap-mcp/ — but do NOT build it before the citation-grammar gap is resolved (see citation_gap). CORRECTED 2026-07-30 (an earlier revision of this field asserted the wrong mechanism): feeding patent records into role prefetch today does NOT deflate the grounded ratio. citation-gate.js:106-108 builds the cited set solely from extractCitations(reportText), and a patent number matches none of the seven CITATION_PATTERNS, so it is never extracted and never reaches the grounded/ungrounded fork at all. Patent evidence is INVISIBLE to the ratio, not counted against it. The guardrail still stands, for a different and subtler reason — see citation_gap.
patsnap.citation_gap: BLOCKING for engine use, but via INVISIBILITY, not deflation. openclaw-bridge/core/citation-extractor.js:3-27 recognizes exactly seven identifier types — PMID, PubChem CID, NCT, UniProt, ChEMBL, DrugBank, DOI. A patent publication number (e.g. US12458612B2) matches NONE, so it is never extracted into the cited set: not grounded against runtime-retrieved records, not Crossref retraction-screened, and neither raising nor lowering the citation-integrity grade because it was never counted in it. Consequence 1: the 'every claim, sourced' guarantee does NOT extend to patent assertions. Consequence 2 — THE REAL CUSTOMER RISK, and it is the opposite of deflation: a buyer sees an A grade on deliverables/citation-integrity.md sitting beside a patent section and reasonably concludes the patents were graded. They were never counted. Any bundle mixing the two needs an explicit grade-adjacency disclosure. Closing the gap means adding a PATENT pattern to CITATION_PATTERNS PLUS a runtime patent-id grounding source IN THE SAME CHANGE — a pattern without a fetched-id set is the ordering that genuinely deflates, because every patent citation would then report ungrounded and reports would start failing.
patsnap.health_check: patsnap_search({search_strategy:['keyword'], keywords:['CRISPR','base editing'], source:'patent', limit:1}) returns a doc with patent_number, assignees and legal_status
patsnap.registry_note: Registered 2026-07-30 on operator OAuth. Recorded as the anchor capability for the founder/startup-facing positioning question opened the same day — see 01-brand-system/brand-identity-2026-07-29.md.

ctgov-supplemental.purpose: Stop-reason archaeology. Searches ClinicalTrials.gov v2 for TERMINATED/WITHDRAWN/SUSPENDED trials in a condition and returns nctId, overallStatus, phases, the sponsor's whyStopped text, and protocol change-history (version count + most-amended modules). Session-cached; the SAME instance backs both role prefetch and the workflow engine's deliverable re-fetch so graveyard-memo.md renders from the records scout actually grounded on. This is the engine's failed-trial intelligence and the reason AdisInsight was declined.
ctgov-supplemental.health_check: ctgov_stopped_trials({condition:'ovarian cancer'}) returns NCT-traced records carrying whyStopped
ctgov-supplemental.registry_note: Was in tool-prefetch-map.json but declared in NO registry entry — the audit's 'tools in prefetch but not declared' drift. Declared 2026-07-24.

ctgov-design-benchmark.purpose: Comparative Phase 3 trial STRUCTURE. Searches ClinicalTrials.gov v2 for the comparable-program cohort in an indication and returns, per program, allocation / masking / intervention model / primary purpose / arm count / enrollment count+type / primary outcome measures with timeframes / lead sponsor + sponsor class / start + primary-completion dates — all in ONE search call, no per-study round-trip. Sibling of ctgov-supplemental (which asks what DIED and why); this asks how the survivors are BUILT. Session-cached, and the SAME instance backs both role prefetch and the workflow engine's post-gate render so deliverables/design-benchmark.{md,csv} render from exactly the records the analyst was grounded on. This is the fulfillment path for the Trial Design Benchmark Pack ($4,950) — before 2026-07-30 that SKU had no template, no mission template and no intake path.
ctgov-design-benchmark.selection_rule: EXPLICIT AND PART OF THE PRODUCT. Sends filter.overallStatus=COMPLETED,ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING,RECRUITING,ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION and sort=StartDate:desc, and returns both to the renderer, which prints them. Verified live 2026-07-30: the unfiltered query reports totalCount 1014 for non-small cell lung cancer and the filtered one 668 — so ~34% of an unfiltered 'eligible' denominator would be withdrawn/terminated/suspended/unknown or never started, and an unsorted page returned a 1995 trial with status UNKNOWN plus a WITHDRAWN trial with enrollment 0. A stated slice is the deliverable; an arbitrary page is not.
ctgov-design-benchmark.health_check: ctgov_design_benchmark({condition:'non-small cell lung cancer'}) returns 20 records carrying nctId + allocation + enrollmentCount, with a non-enumerable eligibleTotal of ~668
ctgov-design-benchmark.registry_note: Added 2026-07-30 with the trial-design-benchmark workflow template. Default pageSize is 20, deliberately NOT the 8 used by ctgov_stopped_trials — that default would silently under-deliver against a pack promising a 10-20 program cohort.

needs_host_auth.note: Connected but UNAUTHENTICATED as of 2026-07-24. Tools unavailable until the operator completes OAuth in claude.ai connector settings (or /mcp in an interactive session). Claude cannot run these flows in a non-interactive session. NOTE: most of what these plugin bundles provide are SKILLS, which need no connection and already work — only the MCP servers listed here need auth.

plugin_surfaces.rationale: Ledger of every Claude PLUGIN bound to this business. A plugin is not a connector — it is a bundle of skills plus (usually) a set of MCP servers. The skills work with no authentication at all; only the MCP servers need OAuth. Recorded here so 'which plugins are configured' is answerable alongside 'what is connected', and so no plugin MCP server drifts into research prefetch. Per-plugin category bindings, posture, and guardrails live in config/plugin-bindings.json (schema plugin-bindings-v1) with the human-readable companion at PLUGIN-BINDINGS.md.
plugin_surfaces.placeholder_model: Plugin packages ship generic `~~category` placeholders (203 across the installed set) that each deployment resolves to its own tools. Unresolved placeholders are the real risk: a skill handed a missing tool invents a plausible substitute. plugin-bindings.json resolves every category, including ~20 that resolve to an explicit NONE.

install_surfaces.desktop-rpm: Materialized per-session under ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/<uuid>/<uuid>/rpm/plugin_*/. Session-scoped, cloud-synced, outside git — NOT durably editable, which is why bindings are repo-owned.

plugins.duplicate_note: Claude-host duplicates of already-registered engine connectors. Interactive/chat-side only — the engine keeps its own subprocess adapters under openclaw-bridge/mcp/. Do NOT double-register and do NOT add to tool-prefetch-map.json: doing so would dilute the grounded-citation ratio the Phase-30 gate computes.

plugins.note: Placeholder-free and fully authenticated — usable as-is.

Resolves ~~design / ~~design tool — there is no Figma.

installed_not_bound.reason: Plugin-authoring tooling. Its cowork-plugin-customizer skill requires Cowork's mnt/.local-plugins mounts, absent in CLI Claude Code — the reason these bindings are repo-owned rather than stamped into the plugin packages.

removed.removed_by: operator, via the Claude Desktop plugin UI
removed.reason: Superseded by the FilesystemPlus MCP server. The operator had already removed desktop-commander from BOTH host configs (~/.claude.json and claude_desktop_config.json) — but the plugin re-registered it from inside its own package, so the removal did not take.
removed.mechanism: It declared `desktop-commander` (`npx -y @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander@latest`) INLINE under mcpServers in .claude-plugin/plugin.json — the only plugin of the 13 to do so, rather than in a sibling .mcp.json. A plugin package is therefore a THIRD MCP registration surface, independent of both host configs.
removed.risk_it_carried: Unpinned @latest third-party npm package providing terminal execution, process management and filesystem access OUTSIDE the sudo-gate / YubiKey model. Confirmed live, not theoretical: 26 mcp__plugin_desktop-commander_* tools loaded in a 2026-07-28 session, and @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander-0.2.46.tgz was present in the npm cache.
removed.verification: 2026-07-28 post-removal, six checks all green: package dir gone; no package named desktop-commander (12 remain); absent from rpm manifest.json (13 -> 12); inline-MCP detector reports 0 across 12 packages; both host configs still clean; no process running.
removed.do_not_reinstall: FilesystemPlus (roots /Users/myhome + /Volumes/ExtraCurricular) covers the filesystem role. If this is ever reinstalled, `node scripts/audit-connector-coverage.js` will flag the inline declaration again — that warning is the tripwire, do not suppress it.
removed.record_correction: The 2026-07-24 enumeration read only .mcp.json and therefore recorded this plugin as having ZERO MCP servers. That was the blind spot; the audit now scans both declaration sites.
